transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Sophia Martinez (Lumenlytics ML Eng), Tom Becker (Lumenlytics Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Lumenlytics Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in to review cache hit rate and tuning options, decide next experiments.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Can everyone hear me?
[00:08] Sophia: yep, good here.
[00:09] Tom: audible, thanks.
[00:12] Maya: cool. Quick agenda: review last week's changes (prefix bucketing + TTL update), look at hit-rate numbers, discuss eviction policy, agree next runs. Ravi will lead hit-rate deep dive. Diego will surface the support ask.
[00:27] Ravi: thanks. Quick TL;DR: after the prefix normalization and adding the 30s soft TTL for session prompts we saw a global KV hit rate jump from ~38% to ~52% across sampled traffic — but it's uneven. Some tenants jump to 70% while others stay under 30%.
[00:44] Sophia: that's roughly what we saw in staging too, the big uplift happens for chat-style sessions where prompts are very repetitive. For our transactional flows the prompts vary more.
[00:52] Maya: do you have a breakdown by route or model?
[00:56] Ravi: yes, I pulled per-route: chat-route-A is 72% after changes, summarization-route-B still 24%. The main factor is prompt canonicalization — we're missing prefix collapse for some templates. Also the KV k key size: some of the keys are big because they include metadata; origin system adds trace IDs which break reuse.
[01:18] Priya: right, we discovered our frontend attaches a request-id header that ends up in the prompt build for a subset of flows. We're cleaning that up.
[01:25] Tom: we will remove request-id from prompt text for reuse flows; infra will ensure the header is preserved in logs but not folded into cached keys.
[01:31] Maya: great. On eviction policy, current POC default is LRU with a fairly large max size. We proposed a hybrid LRU+TTL where frequently used prefixes stay but we evict stale long-tail ones. Thoughts?
[01:44] Ravi: from the sim we ran, pure LRU favors very bursty tenants and starves long-tail prefixes. Hybrid TTL lets us reclaim space from older prefixes that haven't been touched in X minutes. We tried TTL=10m and saw a modest improvement in global hit rate and much better stability under load.
[02:03] Sophia: can we make TTL per-tenant? Some customers have daily workflows that still benefit from long TTLs.
[02:09] Ravi: yes, we support per-tenant policy in the runtime, that's part of Redwood Dedicated's config model. The only catch is each extra policy adds to config surface area for your infra team.
[02:20] Tom: with per-tenant TTLs, what about total memory footprint and OOM risk? We need predictable tail latencies.
[02:27] Ravi: good question. We'll add a safety cap on memory and a reactive eviction backstop that kicks in before OOM — essentially a max-resident-buffers knob plus eviction aggressiveness scale. We can expose a headroom metric in the console.
[02:39] Diego: also want to call out the prefetch heuristic we experimented with: we added a small lookahead for likely next prompts based on user path and warmed the KV for those. That gave a small hit uplift (~3-5%) for flows with predictable next steps.
[02:53] Priya: that prefetch sounds promising but any risk to data residency or sending sensitive content to cache?
[02:59] Maya: we already tag cached entries with customer scope and encryption; but good reminder — prefetching must respect PII redaction and your tenant policies. We can add filters to prevent prefetch on prompts marked sensitive.
[03:11] Sophia: ok. Back to metrics, can you walk through the new sheet Ravi?
[03:15] Ravi: sure I'll share the link after the call but quick numbers: baseline week A avg latency token generation 120ms/seq, cost per 1M tokens $X (redacted here), after the prefix normalization and 30s TTL we see 16% reduction in average tokens per request because fewer repeated prefixes are hit, and estimated cost delta is -11% for the high-hit tenants.
[03:37] Tom: those cost numbers look optimistic — are they assuming warm KV cache across all replicas? What about cross-region egress when prefetching?
[03:44] Ravi: the model has two scenarios: local prefetch only and aggressive cross-region prefetch. The -11% assumes local prefetch and reused KV within the same region. Cross-region prefetch increases egress and can neutralize savings. We've flagged that in the spreadsheet.
[03:58] Maya: action for Tom to validate cross-region constraints.
[04:02] Tom: noted.
[04:05] [04:05] Speaker 1 (automatic): um yeah sorry scratch that, I was muted.
[04:10] Sophia: one pain point: eviction makes debugging harder because sometimes a prompt is evicted and subsequent requests go cold which spikes latency — we need better telemetry to correlate misses to eviction events.
[04:21] Ravi: agreed. We'll add a miss-cause label to logs: cold_start, eviction_ttl, eviction_lru, and provide a trace id mapping so you can see why a miss happened. That will be in the next SDK patch.
[04:33] Priya: how soon can we get that? It's important for our SREs.
[04:36] Diego: aiming for end of next week for the log labels and a small dashboard. I'll coordinate with Ravi.
[04:42] Maya: good. Any perf regressions from the soft TTL change in p99?
[04:47] Ravi: p50 improved, p95 unchanged, p99 had a few spikes when eviction and prefetch overlapped under heavy concurrency — we traced to a lock contention in the local cache layer. We have a kernel path fix that should reduce that; we'll deploy to staging today.
[05:05] Sophia: please keep us posted on that fix. We had one production spike on Wednesday that matched that pattern.
[05:10] Ravi: yes that's likely the same.
[05:12] Maya: next big experiment proposal: run a warmup simulation where we replay 10k anonymized requests to estimate steady-state hit rate under different eviction policies: LRU, TTL=10m, hybrid LRU+TTL, and LRU with targeted prefetch. We want per-route and per-tenant breakdowns.
[05:28] Tom: I can pull 10k traces. We'll anonymize user IDs and drop any PII.
[05:32] Sophia: we'll also include top 10 prompt templates so you can canonicalize prefixes properly.
[05:36] Maya: perfect. We'll run the sims and return numbers. Expected outputs: hit-rate curves over time, memory footprint, latency distribution, and cost delta.
[05:45] Priya: is there a recommended canonicalization approach? We had multiple ways to normalize prompts — stripping timestamps, removing random IDs, etc. Which pattern gives best reuse?
[05:53] Ravi: in our tests, a three-stage normalization works best: 1) structural canonicalization (transform JSON/templated prompts to canonical skeleton), 2) token-level normalization (strip variable tokens like IDs/dates), 3) semantic heuristics (optional, domain-specific rules). We'll share a short cookbook for your templates.
[06:10] Sophia: would love that cookbook.
[06:12] Maya: we'll attach it to the hit-rate sheet. It'll include a few regex examples and pitfalls.
[06:18] [06:18] Speaker 2: quick question, are we comfortable with the cost model assumptions on GPU vs CPU inference?
[06:23] Ravi: for the POC we're using Redwood Hosted GPU assumptions for token cost, but we can swap to your on-prem numbers or Redwood Dedicated numbers if you want; the sheet is parametrized.
[06:33] Tom: please set a scenario for Dedicated with reserved capacity (committed monthly) because that's the direction we may take.
[06:38] Maya: will do.
[06:40] Diego: one more ops note: when we enable per-tenant TTLs we recommend a canary period and a rollout window — start with 5% of traffic, monitor eviction miss causes and p99, then 25% etc. We'll help run the canary.
[06:53] Priya: good, we prefer a slow ramp for infra safety.
[06:57] Maya: ok open questions before we recap?
[07:00] Sophia: curious if there are existing heuristics in the runtime to detect when prefix canonicalization is failing (like a high entropy key distribution) so you can auto-suggest templates.
[07:10] Ravi: we have a key entropy diagnostic that flags high-cardinality keys; we can surface top offenders. Not full auto-suggest yet but it's on the roadmap.
[07:19] Priya: that roadmap item would be huge for our product team.
[07:23] Maya: recap / next steps: 1) Lumenlytics to provide anonymized 10k traces + top prompt templates (Sophia/Tom) by 2026-04-13. 2) Redwood (Ravi) will run sims across four eviction configs and share updated hit-rate sheet and cost projections by 2026-04-14. 3) Maya will send the cookbook + spreadsheet link by 2026-04-09. 4) Tom to validate cross-region prefetch constraints and network egress by 2026-04-10. 5) Diego/Ravi to add miss-cause labels and EV dashboard by end of next week.
[07:58] Tom: confirmed.
[08:00] Sophia: confirmed.
[08:02] Maya: perfect, I'll follow up with calendar invites for the sim results deep-dive and the session affinity meeting. Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[08:10] [08:10] Call ends.
